title: Data Plane Utilities
author: theasianpianist
body:
Methods to send and verify data plane traffic:

1. Send traffic from the T1 to the server after performing some action. Verify: server received packet in time, did/did not receive IP-in-IP tunnel packet on T1
2. Send traffic from the server to the T1 after performing some action. Verify: T1 received packet in time

Depends on #2754, #2816

Summary: Data plane I/O utilities and fixtures for dual-TOR tests
Fixes: https://github.com/Azure/sonic-mgmt/issues/2759

### Type of change

<!--
- Fill x for your type of change.
- e.g.
- [x] Bug fix
-->

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] Test case(new/improvement)

### Approach
Utilities for dualTOR data plane testing. At high level, this PR provides two utilities for the Dual tor tests to consume:
1. `send_t1_to_server_after_action` - simulate data plane traffic from T1 router to server
2. `send_server_to_t1_after_action` - simulate data plane traffic from server to T1 router


#### What is the motivation for this PR?

#### How did you do it?
The utilities are provided as fixtures which yield the data-plane-io functionality to be used within tests.
The I/O test runs mostly on sonic-mgmt-container utilizing the PTF-adapter utility, except the sniffer part, which runs on the PTF container due to permission issues and socket ports that scappy sniffer demands.

Two types of I/O support is provided in two directions - T1 to server, and server to T1.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Tested on a single TOR setup, and the traffic disruptions are successfully captured. Also tried with non-disruptive test, and no disruption and packet loss was seen. Sample tests used are below:

```Python
def try_config_reload(duthost):
    config_reload = duthost.shell("config reload -y")['stdout']
    logger.info("Output of action: {}".format(config_reload))


def try_bgp_summary(duthost):
    show_bgp_summary = duthost.shell("show ip bgp summary")['stdout']
    logger.info("Output of action: {}".format(show_bgp_summary))


def test_t1_to_server_active_tor_config_reload(duthosts, rand_one_dut_hostname, send_t1_to_server_after_action):
    duthost = duthosts[rand_one_dut_hostname]
    
    logger.info("Active ToR before {}".format(duthost.hostname))

    tor_port = 29
    send_t1_to_server_after_action(duthost,
                                tor_port=tor_port,
                                action = lambda: try_config_reload(duthost))
    # TODO add more verification steps here

    logger.info("Active ToR after {}".format(duthost.hostname))

def test_server_to_t1_active_tor_bgp_summary(duthosts, rand_one_dut_hostname, send_server_to_t1_after_action):
    duthost = duthosts[rand_one_dut_hostname]
    #active_host_before = get_active_torhost()
    logger.info("Active ToR before {}".format(duthost.hostname))

    # perform bgp shutdown on active TOR
    send_server_to_t1_after_action(duthost,
                                action = lambda: try_bgp_summary(duthost))
    # TODO add more verification steps here

    logger.info("Active ToR after {}".format(duthost.hostname))
```

This is ready for merge now. The code has been tested with the switchover scenario, finally. Upon simulating a switchover, the traffic was disrupted for 0.071s (<1s), and 19 packets were lost.
